verses.zh: （大卫的记念诗，交与伶长。）　神啊，求你快快搭救我！耶和华啊，求你速速帮助我！
verses.en: For the music director, by David; written to get God’s attention.[NOTE:1] O God, please be willing to rescue me.[NOTE:2] O Lord, hurry and help me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 70. This psalm is almost identical to Ps 40:13-17. The psalmist asks for God’s help and for divine retribution against his enemies.

Heb “to cause to remember.” The same form, a Hiphil infinitive of זָכַר (zakhar, “remember”), also appears in the superscription of Ps 38. Some understand this in the sense of “for the memorial offering,” but it may carry the idea of bringing one’s plight to God’s attention (see P. C. Craigie, Psalms 1-50 [WBC], 303).
Heb “O God, to rescue me.” A main verb is obviously missing. The verb רָצָה (ratsah, “be willing”) should be supplied (see Ps 40:13). Ps 40:13 uses the divine name “Lord” rather than “God.”

verses.zh: 愿那些寻索我命的，抱愧蒙羞；愿那些喜悦我遭害的，退后受辱。
verses.en: May those who are trying to take my lifebe embarrassed and ashamed.[NOTE:1] May those who want to harm mebe turned back and ashamed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “hurry to my help.” See Pss 22:19; 38:22.
Heb “may they be embarrassed and ashamed, the ones seeking my life.” Ps 40:14 has “together” after “ashamed,” and “to snatch it away” after “my life.”

verses.zh: 愿那些对我说阿哈、阿哈的，因羞愧退后。
verses.en: May those who say, “Aha! Aha!”be driven back[NOTE:1] and disgraced.[NOTE:2]
notes: See Ps 35:4 for a similar prayer.tn The four prefixed verbal forms in this verse are understood as jussives. The psalmist is calling judgment down on his enemies.
The prefixed verbal form is understood as a jussive in this imprecation.

verses.zh: 愿一切寻求你的，因你高兴欢喜；愿那些喜爱你救恩的，常说：当尊　神为大！
verses.en: May all those who seek you be happy and rejoice in you.May those who love to experience[NOTE:1] your deliverance say continually,[NOTE:2] “May God[NOTE:3] be praised!”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “May they be turned back according to their shame, those who say, ‘Aha! Aha!’” Ps 40:15 has the verb “humiliated” instead of “turned back” and adds “to me” after “say.”
Heb “those who love,” which stands metonymically for its cause, the experience of being delivered by God.
The three prefixed verbal forms prior to the quotation are understood as jussives. The psalmist balances out his imprecation against his enemies with a prayer of blessing on the godly.
Ps 40:16 uses the divine name “Lord” here instead of “God.”

verses.zh: 但我是困苦穷乏的；　神啊，求你速速到我这里来！你是帮助我的，搭救我的。耶和华啊，求你不要耽延！
verses.en: I am oppressed and needy.[NOTE:1] O God, hurry to me.[NOTE:2] You are my helper and my deliverer.O Lord,[NOTE:3] do not delay.
notes: The prefixed verbal form is taken as a jussive, “may the Lord be magnified [in praise].” Another option is to take the verb as an imperfect, “the Lord is great.” See Ps 35:27.
Ps 40:17 has “may the Lord pay attention to me.”
